fit: ginger-containing decoction and stride in a Parkinson mouse model
assessment: CatWalk Figure 3L shows longer stride in medium and high whole-decoction groups than MPTP controls. The nine-component recipe includes ginger rhizome and has no isolated ground ginger group.

fit: ginger root extract dose comparisons in cohorts including Parkinson disease
assessment: Change in MDS-UPDRS Parts I–IV is listed among its other outcomes. No separate stride-length measure, inactive comparator or posted results were verified.

fit: fragrant sumac bark pumpkin oil and hop trial with planned urgency diary
assessment: Only seven active and two placebo participants received treatment. Early termination left urgency efficacy analysis unreported. The 2019 uncontrolled report is a separate cohort and the bark differs from culinary ground fruit.

fit: levodopa dyskinesia and a TRPV1 antagonist combination in rats
assessment: URB597 plus capsazepine reduced graded abnormal movements. The protocol did not administer capsaicin or cayenne. Isolated capsaicin in the related Lee report measured different hyperactivity outcomes.

fit: ground cayenne served in a controlled breakfast without target clinical measurements
assessment: The same-accession thesis names cayenne powder and compares metabolic outcomes in healthy adults. Fixed meal order conflicts with registered random allocation. Dyskinesia was unmeasured.

fit: sesame oil swishing and speech difficulty ratings in oral submucous fibrosis
assessment: The original table has inconsistent arm totals and gives no reliable between-arm speech estimate. The study does not verify consumption, toasted preparation, Parkinson disease or listener intelligibility.

fit: sesame oil odor in a community smell assay
assessment: The oil substituted for coffee as a test odor. The study provides a measure of sensory recognition without assigned ingestion or preparation-specific effect.

fit: diagnostic sesame-oil odor in Parkinson and multiple system atrophy
assessment: Correct identification was 44.4% in Parkinson disease and 100% in seven multiple system atrophy comparators (p=.010). This does not measure a change from consuming oil.

fit: intranasal sesame oil with respiratory and sleep outcomes
assessment: The original Methods and tables do not provide a measured change in olfactory function. The healthy study uses nasal exposure and no oral sesame comparison.

fit: sesame-labeled stimulus in Parkinson olfactory screening
assessment: The sesame stimulus had AUC 0.655 during discovery. An odor diagnostic contrast does not establish effect of oral cold-pressed oil.

fit: probiotic drops with reported soybean vehicle and stimulated saliva
assessment: Stimulated flow rose in both periodontal trial arms. The original abstract does not identify the oil. Soybean vehicle is secondary attribution, refining is unverified, and drooling is distinct from stimulated flow.

fit: avocado oil mayonnaise in a broader ketogenic case description
assessment: The uncontrolled Down syndrome and Alzheimer case included avocado-oil mayonnaise. Improvement in anxiety was qualitative. Neither a refined oil comparison nor Parkinson disease was present.

fit: ketogenic diet and measured Parkinson anxiety with unisolated oil exposure
assessment: The seven-person continuation reports mean PAS change −6.29 (p=.0313). A participant mentions coconut or avocado oil. The reported exposure, change, control and preparation do not allow an oil-specific effect.

fit: Concord grape juice and grooved pegboard in a healthy crossover
assessment: Juice was slower than placebo in phase one (63.2 vs 60.4 s), with no clear difference in phase two. This is a phase-specific processed juice comparison in healthy adults.

fit: purified grape seed extract and simple finger movement rate
assessment: Baseline-adjusted estimates at weeks 6 and 12 were 123.24 to 125.71 with extract and 124.36 to 121.43 with placebo (interaction p=.005). The follow-up describes placebo decline and maintained extract performance. Complex results were inconclusive. The manuscript Methods match the CP9700 registry despite a conflicting cover ID.

fit: bilberry and grape juice with dominant-hand pegboard
assessment: The mixed juice versus placebo study reports an inconclusive dominant-hand comparison (p=.41). It does not isolate raw grape intake.

fit: grape seed extract and a planned bilateral finger tapping outcome
assessment: The linked 2026 Papa subset publication reports continuous performance and mood. The registered motor result remains unverified.

fit: grape powder and planned grip and pinch strength
assessment: A single-group trial combines grape powder with water. No numerical hand-strength result, raw-fruit contrast or Parkinson cohort was verified.

fit: oral tarragon tincture and rodent wake behavior with unresolved drug-induced sleep assays
assessment: The proceedings report higher early exploration and rearing under oral tincture. The dissertation synopsis labels sedation and references drug-induced sleep experiments without tarragon-specific timing results. Neither evaluates fresh tarragon or clinical daytime sleepiness.

fit: oral avocado-oil comparator and Visual Analog Mood Scale tranquility in healthy adults
assessment: Mean tranquility was 297.3 to 301.3 in the mint-flavored avocado oil arm and 303.0 to 302.4 with CBD, baseline-adjusted p=.85. This short-term proxy gives no verified refined grade, oil-free comparison or Parkinson anxiety result.

fit: groups sofrito and motivation within a Parkinson diet-pattern analysis
assessment: Adjusted diet scores were inversely associated with lack of motivation. The sofrito item permits tomato sauce, gives no isolated leek result and was tested against total symptom burden, not an apathy endpoint.

fit: ground white mustard in a combined Parkinson tea and an illustrative smell trajectory
assessment: The illustrative subject recorded smell severity zero before and throughout treatment. The 17 selected follow-up cases do not supply a group smell estimate. Ground white mustard was combined with broccoli seed and never compared on its own.
